service.description: The identity and scope of a gateway. The gateway must be a Device with a PhysicalDevice and a DgmpEdgeGateway member of at least one DeviceGroup (statusId empty or DgmsAlive). Its scope is those groups and their alive members, recursively; the controllers of the scope are the members with a controller purpose (DgmpProcessPLC, DgmpSafetyPLC, DgmpController, DgmpMotionController, DgmpRemoteIO, DgmpSafetyRemoteIO, DgmpExtremeConditionRemoteIO).

set.value: No gateway identity: set the property device_gateway_device_id.
Configured gateway ${gatewayDeviceId} does not exist as Device + PhysicalDevice.
Gateway ${gatewayDeviceId} is not assigned to any DeviceGroup as DgmpEdgeGateway.

service.description: The subscriptions and polling a gateway starts: the active (fromDate, thruDate) DeviceRequest records of type DrtSubscribe, DrtEvent, DrtStateChange or DrtCyclic, or DrtRead with a pollingInterval, whose device is a controller in the scope of the gateway (get#GatewayScope); ordered by priority, sequenceNum, requestName.

Keeps the subscriptions and polling reads of this gateway (get#StartupSubscriptions, discovered on the first successful call of the process) running, whatever their driver: after a start, and after a fault. On every call it asks DeviceServices.run#DeviceRequest for each of them; the implementation answers unchanged for one that is running and starts one that is not. A failure is tried again after retryDelayMillis; the scheduled job calls it every minute and no service thread sleeps between attempts. maxAttempts is the total of a failure cycle, not a new budget on every call: an exhausted request waits for a restart of the process, a new subscribe, or a call with a higher maxAttempts. An explicit unsubscribe stops the restoration of that request. The property device_gateway_restore_subscriptions=false turns it off for this instance.

Called by DeviceServices.run#DeviceRequest after a subscription, polling or unsubscribe request: a completed DrtUnsubscribe stops the restart of parentRequestName by start#Subscriptions, an active or unchanged subscription or polling resumes it.

Tells the users, with a notification on the topic DeviceInboundFailed or DeviceInboundRecovered, that the samples of a subscription or polling request have failed to store for device_gateway_error_notification_seconds (inboundError), or store again after such a notice (inboundRecovered). Called by the persistence worker.

service-call.name: moqui.device.DeviceServices.send#DeviceNotification
service-call.in-map: {deviceId:deviceId, topic:(failing ? 'DeviceInboundFailed' : 'DeviceInboundRecovered'), requestName:requestName, eventType:eventType, title:(failing ? 'Device data not stored' : 'Device data stored again') + ' (' + requestName + ')', text:failing ? ('The values of request ' + requestName + ' have not been stored for ' + (errorDurationSeconds || 0) + ' s: ' + (errorMessage || 'unknown error')) : ('The values of request ' + requestName + ' are stored again after ' + (errorDurationSeconds || 0) + ' s of errors.')}

service-call.name: moqui.device.DeviceServices.send#DeviceNotification
service-call.in-map: {deviceId:request.deviceId, topic:'DeviceInboundFailed', requestName:requestName, eventType:'acquisitionError', title:'Device acquisition error (' + requestName + ')', text:errorMessage}

service.description: Store logical samples of declared request items. Only DrpLogging creates ParameterLog; a missing purpose updates current Parameter values, writing only the last value of each parameter. Samples are written in chunks of 1000, one transaction each: the reads first, then the writes sent together, as a data load does. Results preserve input order; malformed or out-of-scope rows do not suppress later valid rows. When a chunk fails and the database answers, its samples are stored one by one to isolate the failing row. When the database does not answer, retryable is true and nothing from retryFromIndex on is stored: the caller keeps those samples (an MQTT session keeps them unacknowledged in the broker) and sends them again. A log row with the device-stamped sourceTime, or the sequenceNum, of a row already stored is a duplicate, not an error: a broker redelivers what was stored but not yet acknowledged. Use after#Samples for failure-isolated after-store extensions.

parameter.name: samples
parameter.description: Maps: deviceId, parameterId, value, optional sourceTime and receivedTime (timestamps), quality, optional log sequenceNum. Numeric values remain decimals.

parameter.name: acquisitionErrors
parameter.description: Transport/decode errors reported without dropping valid samples.

parameter.name: notifyErrors
parameter.description: False when the continuous host supplies its rate-limited health notifier.

parameter.name: retryable
parameter.description: The database did not answer: the samples from retryFromIndex on were not stored and are to be sent again.

service.description: Store decoded diagnostic events: ParameterLog for an exact parameterId, otherwise DeviceLog. The device must be the request owner or an alive descendant in its explicit device group hierarchy. Optional logValueKind is numeric, enumeration or message. Events always create logs. This service performs no wire-format decoding and needs no driver installed.
Extension hook after a successful sample batch has committed. Attach SECAs here for local after-store callbacks. Hook errors are logged and isolated from the saved data and persistence health.
